title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

reading.body:
This is an insider misuse case, not a model error. A person with legitimate access to law enforcement systems used that access for a purpose the systems were not deployed for. The tools named are a camera system, a tag reader system, and a state crime database, all built for police work and all reachable by a sworn officer through ordinary credentials. The failure sits at the point of use, where authority to query is granted by role rather than by case.

Catching this kind of misuse is hard because the queries themselves look valid. The controls that would have helped are audit trails tied to individual accounts, review of lookups that cannot be matched to an open case, and alerts when one officer repeatedly queries the same person or plate. The reporting does not say which of these existed at the Coffee County sheriff's office, so what monitoring was in place is not established.

The indictment alleges eight counts, including violation of oath, computer invasion of privacy, prohibited use of captured license plate data, and stalking. An indictment is a charge, not a finding of guilt, and the outcome of the case is not established by these reports.

reports.title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

summary:
A former Coffee County sheriff's deputy, Chris Ashley Rozar, 49, has been released on bond after a grand jury indicted him on eight counts. The charges include four counts of violation of oath by a public officer, two counts of computer invasion of privacy, one count of prohibited use of captured license plate data, and one count of stalking. Investigators say he misused the sheriff's office camera system, tag reader system, and a state crime database for personal reasons, including tracking a woman without her consent. The woman spoke anonymously, saying she hopes her story helps other women report abuse.

Rozar was arrested on May 5 and released on bond the same day. The indictment alleges some incidents happened between April 10 and May 1, 2024. The GBI investigated after former Sheriff Doyle Wooten requested an independent inquiry, and Rozar was fired when the investigation began. He is scheduled for arraignment on May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court.
